<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="PubMed-not-MEDLINE" Owner="NLM"><PMID Version="1">42977802</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>2026</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>03</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2026</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>06</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Electronic"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Print">2397-768X</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Print"><Volume>10</Volume><Issue>1</Issue><PubDate><Year>2026</Year><Month>Oct</Month><Day>13</Day></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>NPJ precision oncology</Title><ISOAbbreviation>NPJ Precis Oncol</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Intratumoral co-activation of ERV transcription and RNA virus-sensing is associated with radiotherapy-induced immune response and abscopal effect.</ArticleTitle><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">421</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1038/s41698-026-01715-4</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Radiotherapy (RT) transforms tumors into in situ vaccines that trigger antitumor immunity. However, the relevant pathways remain largely unelucidated, limiting clinical translation. Herein, we developed a hybrid dry-lab/wet-lab approach integrating systems-level immune phenotypes following homogenous or spatially fractionated RT (SFRT) with transcriptomic profiling of irradiated tumors. By combining feature extraction with machine-learning, including multilayer perceptron modeling, we ranked predictors of immune infiltration and patient survivability for each RT type. RT induced coordinated upregulation of viral RNA-binding proteins (OASes and RIG I-like receptors) along with endogenous retrovirus (ERV) RNAs predominately 400-800&#x2009;bp long, which may serve as their ligands. During abscopal responses, OASes and ERV transcripts were co-induced and shared between irradiated and distant tumors. SFRT triggered earlier activation of OAS signaling versus homogenous RT. Our findings highlight ERVs as underappreciated contributors to RT-induced antitumor immunity and their interactions with intratumoral cytosolic sensors as potential novel biomarkers in precision radio-oncology.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>&#xa9; 2026.
